s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of headache and diplopia with cranial nerve palsies
salient_findings: Right cranial nerve VI and III palsies
key_facts: 70-year-old man
Medical history of atrial fibrillation
Sick sinus syndrome with pacemaker placement
Prostate cancer treated with radiation and hormonal therapy
Obstructive sleep apnea
Left-sided Bell's palsy
Tobacco misuse
Preexisting left-sided incomplete facial nerve palsy
Visual acuity and peripheral vision intact bilaterally
Severe photosensitivity
Normal funduscopic examination
Air fluid levels in bilateral sphenoid and maxillary sinuses on CTA
Irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus on MRI
Left pleural effusion on CT thorax
Mediastinal lymphadenopathy on CT thorax
Mass-like thickening of the posterior left pleura on CT thorax
Mesenteric lymphadenopathy on CT abdomen and pelvis

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of headache and diplopia with cranial nerve palsies, irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus on MRI

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus on MRI, lymphadenopathy on CT scans, and history of prostate cancer

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus on MRI, and cranial nerve palsies

shortlist.label: Metastatic prostate cancer
shortlist.why_kept: History of prostate cancer, and mass-like thickening of the posterior left pleura on CT thorax

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphadenopathy on CT scans, and biopsy of posterior left pleural thickening showed CD5+, CD10−, non-germinal center B-cell type

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of right-sided temporal headache, diplopia, and cranial nerve palsies, combined with the imaging findings of irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus and the biopsy results showing CD5+, CD10−, non-germinal center B-cell type, strongly support the diagnosis of cavernous sinus lymphoma.

rejected.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: While Tolosa-Hunt syndrome can cause similar symptoms, the presence of systemic lymphadenopathy and the specific biopsy results make lymphoma a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus meningioma
rejected.why: Meningioma would not typically cause the systemic findings seen in this patient, such as mediastinal lymphadenopathy and mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

rejected.label: Metastatic prostate cancer
rejected.why: The biopsy results do not support metastatic prostate cancer, and the patient's prostate cancer was treated with radiation and hormonal therapy, making recurrence less likely.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: While lymphoma is a correct diagnosis, it is too broad, and the specific location and type of lymphoma (cavernous sinus lymphoma) make it a more precise champion diagnosis.
